works.abstract: The extensive use of plastics worldwide has led to increasingly severe plastic pollution, posing significant threats to ecosystems and human health. Biodegradable plastics are therefore regarded as an effective way to solve the problem of plastic pollution, because they can be completely degraded into small-molecule substances such as CO2, CH4 and H2O under the action of microorganisms. However, whether complete biodegradation means environmentally friendly remains controversial, because degradation may require specific environmental conditions, take considerable time, and release potentially harmful intermediates before completion. Here we review the definition, types, characteristics, and applications of biodegradable plastics, and discusses their degradation processes and the influencing factors. A focus is placed on the formation of microplastics during the degradation of biodegradable plastics. The effect of biodegradable microplastics on animals, plants, and microorganisms is also evaluated. The current research gaps and shortcomings are identified, and future key research directions are proposed. This review provide a scientific basis for the ecological risk assessment of biodegradable plastics and offers guidance for achieving efficient degradation and science-based management of biodegradable plastics.
works.title: Degradation Processes of Biodegradable Plastics in the Environment and Their Impact on Ecosystems
